The given domain is K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, X=(Gm^2)^an/<(t,2),(3,t)>, with its input compact good strict smooth separated boundaryless pure surface structure. I independently physically read all five fields of all four current421 notes, the entire1797-LF85806-byte standalone, distinct367-LF17296-byte proofs, complete current scopes/ledgers/verdict/residual, three native programs as inert text, and all fifteen complete immediate CLD/GR statement-and-proof units. The exact conventional analytic boundary is CLD v2 15.7.1--3 (separated pure-dimensional calibrated analytic calculus with actual boundary),5.11.1 (smooth Green/Stokes with vanishing boundary here),7.2.8--13 (positive top Radon currents, coefficient measures, multiplication and smooth-test density),8.1.7--8/8.2.4 (entire continuous sheaf, transfinite uniform closure and convex nondecreasing composition),8.5.1/5,8.7.1--2/4,8.8.4--6/8--9 (actual recursive positive closed products, uniform continuity, symmetry, smooth-null changes and coordinate support/dimension),11.6.3/5(c),13.8.1--5,18.6.1--2 (full graded coordinates and fixed finite-flat Gauss fibre currents),14.5.2--3 and5.10.1(c),(d)/5.10.2 (degree/lattice calibration and top Radon reconstruction). The identity moment has saturated primitive lattice and degree1; rawfactor2 is the wedge square factor2!. GR v2 unnumbered Section1.2 gives the CLD-to-classical bridge;4.1--4.2 gives its USC/every-curve/every-extension scope;6.3--6.4 gives full-dimensional finite affinoid Shilov boundaries and their maximum principle. The bounded facts used below were reconstructed, not granted by supplied notes. For a positive closed current T, complete smooth gradients in Q_T(f,g)=int d'f Jd'g T. Closedness and finite coefficient measures show that a uniformly zero sequence with a strong gradient limit has zero limit. Nested cutoffs give, for uniformly convergent bounded psh f_j, Q_(T,chi)(f_j-f_k)<=epsilon^2||DDchi T||TV/2+2A epsilon||chi||infinity||DDeta T||TV. The gradient domain is uniformly closed and includes every continuous stage by minimality. Green then gives Q_T(f,g)=-int f DD(gT) and Q_T(f)>=0. Recursive cubic expansion yields E'=int(b-a)MA(a_t), E''=-2Q_theta_at(b-a), monotonicity/concavity, E(c)=2c, tangent inequality and the exact midpoint gain I(a,b)/8. Thus I<=4(epsilon_a+epsilon_b) for full-dual deficits.

Actual coordinate curves with annulus harmonic interpolation give normalized Gauss restrictions coordinatewise1/2-Lipschitz and in[-1/2,0]. Shrinking polyannuli and their finite Shilov vertices give a(x)<=a(sigma tau x). Strict off-Gauss Laurent cancellation confines the local coordinate tropical image to dimension<=1; top coordinate forms vanish there. Identity calibration gives theta^2=2sigma_*Lebesgue. Fixed coordinate paths/collar caps give finite-grid gradient control. Full-point Laurent Abhyankar coordinates and finite-flat singleton-Gauss representatives give bounded w_x with MA(w_x)>=alpha_x delta_x, alpha_x>0, by the fixed log-max fibre current and collar gluing.

On a common energy sublevel Green gives Q_theta_w(a-b)<=I/2+sqrt(42CI): the two transgression pairings have individual gradient bounds12C+3C+6C=21C. Grid control and a smooth absolute-value ramp give bounded-test L1 moduli tending to zero with I; the atoms force equality of limits at every full point. Also Q_theta_b(a)<=6C gives segment second-derivative bound48C for differences of two sublevel endpoints. Laurent collar caps separate all actual points; span(C) is a vector lattice, and finite max/min interpolation on compact X proves its uniform density in C(X,R). notes.detailedSummary: Proves periodic Alexandrov existence/uniqueness for every Radon probability by compact Laguerre minimization, correct Legendre reversal, null cell boundaries, atomic approximation and proved conjugate-gradient continuity. Actual positive convex convolution, calibrated rawfactor2 and recursive product continuity lift on every continuous analytic test. Normalized range[-1/2,0], energy[-1,0], fullD<=1; actual G presentation, generated uniqueness against bounded solutions, and J=K=0 for every fast family. Explicit2delta_Gauss has E=-1/3,D=1/6. notes.text:
At the explicitly qualified analytic foundation boundary of own n1, every positive raw-mass2 Radon measure mu supported on S=sigma(T), T=R^2/Z^2, has an actual normalized continuous invariant q in the ORIGINAL entire C with MA(q)=mu. Its range is[-1/2,0], E(q) is in[-1,0], and it attains the FULL dual D(mu)<=1. It has an actual decreasing continuous G presentation and is unique modulo constants among ALL actual G solutions with this measure. This is a scoped theorem, not original P16.7 closure. The real construction below is proved independently of any external periodic Alexandrov or transport existence theorem.

Real preliminaries. Let rho(r)=|r|^2/2, Phi=rho+qbar convex with qbar continuous periodic, and Psi=Phi* its Legendre conjugate. Boundedness of qbar gives superlinearity and compact attainment of conjugate suprema. Substituting lattice translations gives Phi(r+k)=Phi(r)+r.k+|k|^2/2 and the same law for Psi. Supporting planes to the finite convex epigraph exist by finite-dimensional separation; they imply biconjugacy and y in partial Phi(r) iff r in partial Psi(y), with Fenchel equality. Comparing a subgradient p at r with r+/-e_i gives |p_i-r_i|<=1/2. Integrating along coordinate lines gives coordinate1/2-Lipschitz qbar, hence normalized oscillation<=1/2 on T. Convex functions are differentiable almost everywhere: one-dimensional left/right derivatives disagree at only countably many points on each coordinate line; Fubini gives partial derivatives almost everywhere; supporting vectors then form a singleton. Locally bounded subgradients and their supporting inequalities show singleton subgradient implies differentiability.

Alexandrov normalization and continuity. Define M_Phi=(gradient Psi mod Z^2)_*Lebesgue_T, where Lebesgue_T has mass1. Gradients are measurable difference-quotient limits off a null set and are translation-equivariant. For Borel E in T choose unique representatives Etilde in[0,1)^2. Outside the null nondifferentiability set and its lattice translates, sum_k 1_(partial Phi(Etilde))(y+k)=1_E(gradient Psi(y) mod Z^2). This follows from Fenchel reciprocity and the unique representative of gradient Psi(y)+k. The subgradient image differs from the measurable inverse-gradient set only on a Lebesgue-null set, so is measurable for completed Lebesgue measure. Integration proves M_Phi(E)=Lebesgue(partial Phi(Etilde)), the ordinary Alexandrov convention WITHOUT factorial, and proves countable additivity. If qbar_n converges uniformly, conjugates satisfy |Psi_n-Psi|<=||qbar_n-qbar|| globally. Their locally bounded gradients have every cluster in partial Psi(y) by passing supporting inequalities to the limit. At common differentiability points that set is a singleton, so gradients converge. Dominated convergence against continuous periodic tests proves M_Phi_n weakly converges to M_Phi. For smooth Phi, M_Phi=det(Hess Phi)dr: strictly positive Hessian gives a lattice-equivariant global gradient diffeomorphism by strong convexity, coercive minimization and the inverse function theorem, followed by change of variables. For merely nonnegative smooth Hessian use (1-epsilon)Phi+epsilon rho and the just-proved continuity.

Finite atomic construction. For P=sum_i m_i delta_xi with distinct torus sites, m_i>0 and sum m_i=1, set c_i(y)=min_k|y-x_i-k|^2/2 and H(w)=int max_i(w_i-c_i(y))dy-sum_i m_i w_i. The torus costs are continuous in[0,1/4]. H is continuous convex and invariant under common weight shifts. On max_i w_i=0, H(w)>=-1/4+sum_i m_i(-w_i). Thus the nonempty sublevel H<=H(0)<=0 is compact, with -1/(4m_i)<=w_i<=0, and H has a global minimum. On each compact set only finitely many nearest copies matter; equality of weighted squared costs of distinct site copies lies in affine hyperplanes. Their countable union is Lebesgue null, so the winning site/copy is unique almost everywhere. Dominated differentiation gives partial H/partial w_i=volume(C_i)-m_i. At the minimum these derivatives vanish. Positive prescribed cell volumes are therefore proved, not assumed.

Define Psi_w(y)=rho(y)+max_i(w_i-c_i(y))=max_(i,k)[(x_i+k).y-|x_i+k|^2/2+w_i]. This is finite convex, locally polyhedral and quasi-periodic. Its conjugate Phi_w is rho plus a continuous periodic function. On C_i, gradient Psi_w is x_i+k almost everywhere, so M_Phi_w=P. The Legendre direction is essential: the TARGET is the Alexandrov measure of Phi_w, not Psi_w. Full cells of individual copies are intersections of plane-winning halfspaces, contained in x_i+k+[-1/2,1/2]^2 because they beat their own neighboring copies. Cells are lattice translates, have null boundaries, and summing their intersections with a fundamental square shows each full cell has volume m_i. Fenchel equality identifies it with partial Phi_w(x_i+k).

All Radon targets and real uniqueness. Approximate any Radon probability P by placing the masses of finite half-open grid squares at sites in those squares, omitting zero masses. Continuous-test errors are bounded by the test modulus at sqrt(2)/n. The normalized atomic potentials have the uniform range and Lipschitz bounds above. A diagonal subsequence on successive finite grids is uniformly Cauchy by the Lipschitz bound, and has continuous periodic limit qbar with rho+qbar convex. Proved Alexandrov continuity gives M_Phi=P. For uniqueness, write two solution pairs as Phi_j=rho+q_j and Psi_j=rho+h_j. Fenchel at all lattice copies gives q_j(x)+h_j(y)+c(x,y)>=0, where c is torus squared distance/2. Gradient Psi_j(y)-y has coordinates in[-1/2,1/2], so this cost equals its actual Euclidean squared cost, and Fenchel equality holds on the gradient plan. Both plans push source Lebesgue to P. Applying each pair's feasible inequality to the other plan proves equality of their costs. The nonnegative slack for pair1 on plan0 therefore vanishes almost everywhere. With the actual nearest lift, gradient Psi_0(y) belongs to partial Psi_1(y), forcing equality of the real gradients at common differentiability points. The locally Lipschitz difference has zero weak gradient by coordinate absolute continuity/Fubini; convolution makes it constant on the connected plane. Conjugation proves q_0-q_1 is constant. No optimal transport existence/uniqueness theorem was invoked.

Actual analytic lift. S is closed and sigma:T->S is a homeomorphism inverse to tau|S, so put P=tau_*mu/2 and take the real solution. Even nonnegative smooth convolution gives periodic qbar_j uniformly converging to qbar, and rho+qbar_j is the convolution of convex Phi minus a constant, hence has I+Hess qbar_j>=0. The functions q_j=qbar_j(tau) have ordinary CLD smooth positive local potentials using the actual invertible z_1,z_2 moments. Deck shifts change the local reference by smooth affine DD-null unit-logarithm combinations; periodicity gives actual quotient gluing. The ORIGINAL minimal continuous-sheaf uniform closure gives q=qbar(tau) in C.

For each smooth approximant the top coordinate form vanishes off S: strict Laurent cancellation persists on an ordinary neighborhood whose coordinate tropicalization lies in a finite dimension<=1 tropical hypersurface. At Gauss points the identity moment has primitive saturated lattice and analytic degree1. The exact calibration/reconstruction applications in n1 and direct wedge expansion therefore give MA(q_j)=2sigma_*[det(I+Hess qbar_j)dr]=2sigma_*M_Phi_j. The factor2 is raw2!, while M_Phi_j has probability mass1. Real continuity makes these actual analytic measures converge to mu against EVERY continuous analytic test h, since h(sigma(r)) is continuous. Independently CLD recursive product continuity gives MA(q_j)->MA(q) as currents; positivity, smooth-test density and common mass2 upgrade this to all continuous tests. Thus the actual original operator satisfies MA(q)=mu; it is not defined by projection or by declaration.

The real normalized bounds hold on ALL X. Energy monotonicity gives -1<=E(q)<=0. Tangent concavity in the ENTIRE C gives E(a)<=E(q)+int(a-q)MA(q), proving FULL-dual attainment. For every normalized a in C its Gauss range is[-1/2,0], so int(-a)mu<=1 and E(a)<=0; hence D(mu)<=1, with the zero competitor giving D>=0. Choose smoothing indices with ||q_j-q||<=2^-j and put b_j=q_j+3*2^-j. Bounds above/below q show b_(j+1)<=b_j and b_j decreases pointwise to q with finite lower energy, an actual original G presentation.

Generated uniqueness is reproved as follows. For c_n decreasing to v with finite lower energy, compact strict domination compares either presentation with a fixed term of the other plus epsilon; monotonicity and E(a+epsilon)=E(a)+2epsilon give canonical limiting energy. The same argument for finite convex combinations, followed by finite unisolvent cubic interpolation, gives coefficient convergence. For fixed bounded w, P_n(t)=E((1-t)c_n+tw) and A_n(t)=E(tc_n) give int w MA(c_n)=P'_n(0)+A'_n(1). Dense tests/Riesz yield the original canonical weak MA(v)=lambda and finite d=lim int c_n MA(c_n). Passing bounded tangent inequalities gives D(lambda)<=e-d. Its dual inequality and sequential monotone convergence give v integrable against lambda. The ordered cocycle bounds 0<=int(c_n-c_l)MA(c_l)<=3(E(c_n)-E(c_l)) for l>=n. Pass l then n to infinity to obtain d=int v lambda, D(lambda)=e-int v lambda, and F_lambda(c_n)->D(lambda).

Normalize by s_n=sup c_n. These decrease to finite s=sup v: E(c_n)<=2s_n bounds them below and nested compact maximum-superlevel sets prove equality. Thus a_n=c_n-s_n converges everywhere to v-s, has bounded lower energy and maximizes D(lambda). If lambda=MA(q), q also attains this dual, so midpoint and n1's full-point moduli give v-s=q at every full point. Such points are dense because every ordinary open contains a pure2 affinoid neighborhood with nonempty full Shilov boundary. USC of v-s prevents it being below continuous q anywhere. Conversely each rho+a_n is bounded by its finite affinoid Shilov maximum; pass n to infinity on that finite boundary, then shrink neighborhoods using continuity of rho+q, to get v-s<=q everywhere. Therefore v=q+s on ALL X. No historical full generated uniqueness or Borel recognition theorem was assumed.

For every fast maximizing family for this mu, midpoint gives I(a_n,q)<=4epsilon_n; the reconstructed moduli give e=E(q), nu=mu and equality at full points. Its all-Shilov relaxation is R=q. Since u<=q and int u mu>=e-D(mu)=int q mu, J=0 and u=q mu-almost everywhere; fixed bounded-product L1 limits give the other bounded MA/mixed almost-everywhere equalities, and K=0. No global positivity is assigned to that Borel u at remaining points.

Exact example: for mu=2delta_sigma(0), xi_i=r_i-floor(r_i), qbar=sum_i xi_i(1-xi_i)/2-1/4. Phi is the sum of the convex piecewise-affine interpolants of r_i^2/2 at integers, minus1/4. Derivative jumps are1, so real Alexandrov measure is delta_0 and actual MA is2delta_sigma(0). Reference/mixed/MA moments are-1/6,-1/3,-1/2, giving E=-1/3 and FULL D=1/6. The mixed measure is the sum of the two coordinate-circle Lebesgue measures, also obtained by actual convolution/product limits. Translations give every Gauss-point atom.

Actual segment variations give gap>=min(Delta/2,Delta^2/(96C0)). A concrete full-dimensional cancellation-point2Dirac is eligible, with dual>=1/6+1/25165824 and no invariant maximizer. notes.text:
Using earlier own n1 and n2, for EVERY eligible arbitrary-support mu let lambda=sigma_*tau_*mu. Then D(mu)>=D(lambda), with equality if and only if mu=lambda. A continuous invariant full-dual maximizer exists exactly for skeletal measures, without the earlier smoothness or positive-definite coordinate-Hessian assumptions. This advances arbitrary-support recognition but does not establish its existence equation.

Proof: Gauss dominance gives int a mu<=int a lambda for every a in C, hence F_mu(a)>=F_lambda(a). The actual skeletal solution q_lambda from n2 is invariant, so F_mu(q_lambda)=D(lambda). If the duals are equal, it attains D(mu). The right derivative on the ACTUAL segment to any a in C is int(a-q_lambda)(lambda-mu)<=0. The invariant term vanishes, giving the inequality opposite to Gauss dominance. Thus all C integrals agree; density of span(C) gives mu=lambda. Conversely equality is immediate for mu=lambda. If any invariant b attains D(mu), then D(mu)=F_lambda(b)<=D(lambda)<=D(mu), forcing skeletal support; n2 supplies the converse existence.

For nonskeletal mu, density supplies an actual a in C with Delta=int a(lambda-mu)>0. Normalize a and q_lambda, and set C0=max(1,-E(a),-E(q_lambda)). Along their actual segment q_t, the bounded Green estimates give |F_mu''(q_t)|<=48C0. Thus F_mu(q_t)>=D(lambda)+t Delta-24C0t^2. Choosing t=min(1,Delta/(48C0)) proves the strictly positive quantitative bound D(mu)-D(lambda)>=min(Delta/2,Delta^2/(96C0)). No arbitrary smooth positivity margin or recovery of lost fibre data is assumed.

A concrete nonskeletal eligible input is mu=2delta_x, where x is the Gauss point of the bidisc z_i=1+s u_i, |u_i|<=1. Independent u_i initials give full graded dimension2; tau(x)=0, while |z_i-1|(x)=exp(-1/8) differs from its norm1 at sigma(0). The local coordinate representative ((z_1-1)/s,(z_2-1)/s) has degree1 near its Gauss image; the fixed log-max fibre current and collar cap give MA(w_x)>=alpha delta_x. Put Bx=D(MA(w_x))<infinity, obtained from bounded tangent concavity. For normalized a, write C=-E(a), A=int(-a)theta^2<=1, q0=Q_theta(a), q1=Q_theta_a(a). Twice integrating E''(ta) gives C=A+2q0/3+q1/3 and -E(ta)=tA+t^2(1-t/3)q0+t^3q1/3<=t+3t^2C/2. Apply the full dual of MA(w_x) to ta, divide by t and optimize to get int(-a)MA(w_x)<=1+Bx+sqrt(6BxC). Consequently F_mu(a)<=-C+(2/alpha)(1+Bx+sqrt(6BxC)), whose supremum is finite. This proves finite FULL dual for this actual nonskeletal Dirac.

In the injective tropical ball |r|<1/4 around0 set psi=log max(1,|z_1-1|/exp(-1/16)) and w=max(0,1/256+psi/64-rho). On its closure psi<=5/16 and w<=9/1024; on |r|>=3/16, rho>=9/512, so w vanishes on an outer collar. Actual log-max approximation, maximum closure and zero gluing give w in C. At sigma(0) and x its values are5/1024 and4/1024. Normalize a=w-sup w; energy monotonicity gives -E(a)<=9/512<1. For lambda=2delta_sigma(0), Delta=1/512 and C0=1. By n2's exact D(lambda)=1/6, D(2delta_x)>=1/6+1/25165824. This mu has no continuous invariant maximizer. A noninvariant solution for it is not constructed here.

There is also stability of the solved sector. Normalized skeletal solutions converge uniformly when their torus probabilities converge weakly: the uniform range/Lipschitz bounds give subsequential compactness; proved real MA continuity identifies every cluster with the limit target; real uniqueness identifies the potential. For coordinate l1 torus distance, each potential is1/2-Lipschitz. Integrating against any coupling of P0,P1 and recalling rawmass2 gives |D(2sigma_*P0)-D(2sigma_*P1)|<=W1(P0,P1). The competing-solution deficit is at most2W1, so midpoint gives I(q0,q1)<=8W1. Taking infima over couplings needs no optimal-coupling existence assumption.
